newsitem.title: MALTA: Maltese tourist project in Albania stalls.
newsitem.headline: Maltese tourist project in Albania stalls.

text.p: A $300 million tourism project in Albania by Malta's AX Holdings tourism and leisure group has been put on hold for up to a year because of the unrest in the former East European country, investor Anglu Xuereb said. MALTESE
Plans and contracts for the building of the holiday resort in the coastal Albanian town of Saranda had just been finalised and work was due to start later this year.

"Despite the turmoil the country is going through, I still strongly believe in the country's potential for investment and in the feasibility of the project," Xuereb told Maltese reporters late on Tuesday.
The resort would have taken three years to built at a cost of $200 million and a further $100 million in Albania, he said.
Xuereb made his statement as a Maltese oil field services company quit the country after its offices were ransacked.
Adrian Said, director of Medserv based in the Albanian port town of Durres two years ago, said the company offices were ransacked on Sunday evening and he was evacuated by U.S. marines.
"Our offices in Durres were destroyed. Anything which could be carried away, including doors and windows, was stolen and the building was stripped bare," he said.
